posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked:
I have an idea of what Vengeance might actually be. I'm in the somewhat rare position of having occassionally been around the designers when they've been talking about their future designs such that it's possible for me to have inside knowledge. On the other hand, my memory can be atrocious, and due to tiredness and distraction I don't always attend very well to what's being said. I remember, for instance, sitting next to Christopher and Adam in our hostel in Seattle for PAX as they talked in some detail about the planned heroes for Shattered Timelines and I was so tired that I completely zoned out and heard nothing of what they were saying.

Or did I?!

As I present my idea of what Vengeance is, maybe it's influenced by what I heard then or other times, w/out being conciously aware of it or remembering it. Keep in mind though, that I am the same person who thought for a long while that Ambuscade was an alien (a la Predator), when he is, in fact, French. (Hmmm ... is that a big difference? I kid, I kid!)

Anyway, here goes my idea: 7 or 11 decks refers to the fact that there are five villain decks that are intended to be played together. Of the other six decks, five of them are new heroes and the remaining one is an environment deck. So far, this is all the same as other people have said. Vengeance, though, also apparently has something cool about its 'components' and 'gameplay', so I found myself wondering what those are. My current guess is that it has something to do with fighting multiple villains at a time -- that the components help you give your battle some sort of spatial arrangement. Maybe one has to keep track of which villain targets one is near or something like that.

So, I don't have a really clear idea of what the new stuff is and I have no idea whether or not it was influenced by anything I might have heard from the designers in the past. It's probably all bunk. Can't wait to learn what Vengeance _actually_ is.

Just for comparisons, although an unfair one…

Shattered Timelines including promo decks has 3 heroes (after hitting 100k), 5 villains, and 3 environments = 11 decks for $20.

And with that 20 dollars you could play a three player game, with a handful of tokens, and have three decks lying around loose. And you already are admitting that the bonus Hero, Villain, Environment and tokens are “unfair” to include as comparison.

With the 30 dollar “Mega-expansion”, I would assume you get 5 heroes, 1 Special Environment (which may or may not be larger then others), 1 Super Deck of Villains that is made up of 5 Villain Decks, with enough tokens to play the game (and I am assuming a 3-5 player game) out of the box, and plenty of space to hold it all.

For 40 Dollars, you can get 10 Heroes, 4 Villains, 4 Environments, enough tokens to play the game 3-5 players and plenty of space to hold it all.

Kickstarter Expansion: 11 Decks and some tokens and a small box (enough to play the smallest recommened game)
Normal Expansion: 8 Decks and a small box (Not enough to play the game)
Mega Expansion: 11 Decks, Tokens and a Large Box (Enough to play the game - I assume full but may just be up to 4)
1st Edition: 18 Decks and an even smaller small box, with out any dividers, so they just jumble up all the freaking time (Enough to play full game)
Enhanced Edition: 18 Decks, Tokens and a Large Box (Enough to play full game)

To me it feels to be the price point feels fine, even with including the Kickstarter extras, but is vastly superior to a normal expansion at the retail level (which is honestly where the comparison should be made).

It also makes me sort of upset I was an early fan of the game. 1st Edition really does sort of suck compared to Enhanced Edition.

Well the only reason why I'm speculating what I have is, it's a "stand alone" expansion.  I don't see how if we change the "Heros" to "Villians" how it would change the game dynamically.  In a nutshell if you really look at it. A villian is just a deck with specific rules with a specific number of hit points which the players whittle down.  The players are just several larger precreated decks which behave in a certain way that is matched up with a fictional character that thematically fits the type of deck played. 

A Stand Alone expansion may allow for some changes - especially with the Villians at the forefront of the expansion, it doesn't mean the gameplay has been changed (for the worse) it could allow for a similar experience (but as bad guys) or even create at the same time set up for a new gaming experience (as in allowing for possible PvP combat)
